pll1d26c4-d1e3501.summary: Asks how being Son of God is proper to the begotten God when humans too are called and are sons of God ('you are all sons of the Most High'; 'Israel is my firstborn').

pll1d26c4-d1e3525.summary: Answers that the difference is great: humans are sons of God by making, not property of birth; the Son is Son by property of origin and truth of nativity, not making or adoption. Humans exist before they become sons; they are made sons, not born.
claims: Humans are sons by making, not birth.
The Son is Son by origin and true birth.

pll1d26c4-d1e3528.summary: Cites Hilary, De Trinitate XII: only the one born of the true Father is truly Son. We are sons by making, once children of wrath, now adopted by grace, acquired not born. Adoptive sonship is appellation, not property, and was not always; the only-begotten was never not Son and is Son by property and truth of birth, and only his begetter is his Father.
claims: Only the one born of the Father is truly Son.
Humans are sons by adoption and grace.

pl-l1d26c4.summary: Asks how being Son of God is proper to the begotten God when humans too are called sons of God (Ps 81:6; Exod 4:22). The difference is great: humans are sons by making and adoption, existing before they become sons; the Son is Son by property of origin and truth of birth. Hilary: we are sons by grace, made and acquired, not born; adopted man is a son by appellation, not property, and was not always son; the only-begotten was never not Son, and only his begetter is his Father.
claims: Humans are sons of God by making and adoption, not by birth.
The Son of God is Son by property of origin and truth of birth.
Humans exist before they become sons; the only-begotten was never not Son.
Adopted sonship is by appellation; the Son's is by property.
